newsitem.title: INDIA: India to speed up power project approvals.
newsitem.headline: India to speed up power project approvals.

text.p: India will set up a committee with powers to give speedy approval to electricity projects, and states will have more decision-making powers to approve power plants, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Wedensday.
He was speaking to state chief ministers at a conference on the power sector.
The prime minister said he favoured an increase in the limit up to which states can approve power projects from the current 10 billion rupees.
"We do not want to centralise the power sector at Delhi," Deve Gowda said.
On environmental approvals, officials told a news conference that Deve Gowda favoured giving more powers to state governments subject to guidelines laid down by the federal government.

Junior power minister S.Venugopalachari said the federal government planned to amend Indian law in the next parliament sesion to give more powers to the states in giving environmental clearance to power projects.
India invited private and foreign investors to set up power projects under an economic reform progamme launched in 1991.
